title: EditDistill: Is It Possible to Guide Video Editing with Image Editing?
title_zh: EditDistill：能否用图像编辑引导视频编辑？

paragraphs.en: Recent advances in image editing have enabled fine-grained and highly controllable visual modifications. However, achieving similar levels of controllability in video editing remains an open challenge, particularly for precise local edits, dynamic temporal effects, and consistent lighting across frames. In this paper, we propose EditDistill , a framework that distills image-level visual transformations from edits to guide video editing. Specifically, given a source video and an edit prompt, we first generate an edited version of the initial video frame using an off-the-shelf image editing model. We then distill the visual transformation of this original-edited image pair into a compact representation termed an edit descriptor . This descriptor is injected into a video diffusion model through our lightweight fusion module, which steers the denoising process toward the desired edit. To align the video trajectory with the demonstrated image edit while preserving motion and layout, we train with edit-descriptor alignment and DINO structural consistency losses, and derive an equivalent inference-time guidance formulation under flow matching. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves strong performance on standard benchmarks and produces high-quality video editing results across diverse scenarios. For more details and videos, please refer to the project webpage: https://yu-shaonian.github.io/EditDistill-Web/ .

paragraphs.en: Recent advances in AI-generated content (AIGC) have led to remarkable progress in both image and video generation. In particular, modern image editing models ( Zhao et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2025a ; Team et al., 2025 ; Team, 2025 ; OpenAI, 2025 ; OpenAI, 2026 ; G. Deepmind, 2025 ) have demonstrated strong capabilities in performing fine-grained and controllable edits, enabling complex local modifications with high fidelity. However, controllable video editing remains significantly more challenging, with existing methods suffering from three interrelated limitations. First, fine-grained local editing, such as modifying object details or attributes, is often unreliable and typically requires explicit masks ( Hu et al., 2025 ) , which are difficult to obtain and maintain across frames. Second, modeling dynamic background effects, such as rain, snow, or other temporally evolving phenomena, remains challenging ( Wu et al., 2023 ) largely due to the lack of explicit temporal control signals. A similar issue was also observed in frame-wise editing methods such as I2VEdit ( Ouyang et al., 2024b ) , which ignore the denoising process alignment during video editing. Third, existing methods struggle to jointly edit foreground and background in a consistent and controllable manner, often leading to inconsistent results ( Jiang et al., 2025 ) . Taken together, these limitations suggest that directly controlling video editing in the video domain is inherently difficult. In contrast, we observe that such complex edits are much easier to achieve in the image domain using modern image editing models. We hypothesize that a single edited reference frame can encode the editing intent, including the visual signature of dynamic effects, while the video diffusion prior supplies the temporal unfolding. paragraphs.en: To this end, we propose EditDistill , a two-stage framework that distills image-level visual transformations from edits into a compact edit descriptor and injects it into video diffusion model for controllable video editing. In the first stage, we utilize powerful image editing models ( e.g. , Qwen-Image ( Wu et al., 2025a ) or GPT-Image-2 ( OpenAI, 2026 ) ) to generate an edited version of the first frame of a given video, based on an edit prompt. Given the original image and the edited image as a pair, we learn a compact edit descriptor that captures the transformation between them. Specifically, this transformation is encoded into a 1024-dimensional latent feature, which serves as guidance for the subsequent video editing process. In the second stage, we inject the edit descriptor into a video diffusion model (Wan 2.1 backbone ( Wang et al., 2025a ) ) through our lightweight fusion module. Combined with the edit descriptor alignment loss, this imposes strong constraints on the denoising trajectory, guiding the model toward the desired editing direction during the denoising process (see Fig. 2 ). As a result, the model can perform fine-grained and controllable video editing without requiring explicit masks. To ensure temporal consistency, we further introduce a feature alignment strategy based on the DINO ( Caron et al., 2021 ) , which aligns frame-level features similarity of the generated video with original video, thereby preserving structural coherence across frames.

paragraphs.en: We introduce image-to-video edit distillation: an image pair demonstrating a visual transformation is compressed into a compact feature and reused as an explicit video editing condition.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出图像到视频的编辑蒸馏（edit distillation）：将展示某种视觉变换的图像对压缩成一个紧凑的特征，并将其作为显式的视频编辑条件复用。

paragraphs.en: We design a parameter-efficient transformation injection mechanism for large video diffusion transformers, combining spatial cross-attention, global FiLM modulation, and additive residual editing while keeping the 14B backbone frozen.
paragraphs.zh: 我们为大型视频扩散 Transformer 设计了一种参数高效的变换注入机制，结合了空间交叉注意力、全局 FiLM 调制和加性残差编辑，同时保持 14B 主干网络冻结。

paragraphs.en: We formulate edit descriptor alignment and DINO structural similarity losses that jointly improve edit fidelity and temporal coherence, and relate them to the gradient guidance during denoising.
paragraphs.zh: 我们设计了编辑描述符对齐损失和 DINO 结构相似性损失，二者共同提升编辑保真度与时序一致性，并将它们与去噪过程中的梯度引导相关联。

paragraphs.en: We curate a five-family video editing dataset and show that EditDistill achieves competitive edit fidelity while improving preservation, temporal consistency, and perceptual quality over the evaluated baselines.
paragraphs.zh: 我们整理了一个包含五个视频编辑家族的数据集，并表明 EditDistill 相较于所评估的基线方法，在实现具有竞争力的编辑保真度的同时，提升了保持性、时序一致性和感知质量。

paragraphs.en: Recent image editing systems have demonstrated that diffusion models can follow rich editing instructions from text or images. Representative approaches include stochastic editing via noisy image trajectories ( Meng et al., 2022 ) , prompt-based editing ( Hertz et al., 2023 ; Brooks et al., 2023 ) , inversion-based control ( Mokady et al., 2023 ) , and latent diffusion models that enable high-resolution synthesis at scale ( Rombach et al., 2022 ) . While these methods achieve strong performance in single-image editing, their control signals are typically defined at the image level, limiting their ability to ensure temporal consistency or to reuse learned transformations across videos. In contrast, our first stage represents an image edit as a compact feature-level transformation, enabling it to serve as a guidance signal for video editing.

paragraphs.en: Video diffusion models provide strong priors for text-to-video and image-to-video synthesis ( Blattmann et al., 2023 ; Wu et al., 2023 ; Khachatryan et al., 2023 ; Guo et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2025a ) . Building controllable editors on top of these priors remains challenging. Existing approaches explore attention control, feature propagation, inversion, correspondence guidance, and one-shot tuning, including Video-P2P ( Liu et al., 2024 ) , TokenFlow ( Geyer et al., 2024 ) , CoDeF ( Ouyang et al., 2024a ) , VideoSwap ( Gu et al., 2024 ) , AnyV2V ( Ku et al., 2024 ) , and RF-Solver-Edit ( Wang et al., 2025b ) . Recent systems broaden the control interface: HunyuanCustom ( Hu et al., 2025 ) targets customized video generation from multimodal reference conditions, while VACE ( Jiang et al., 2025 ) unifies video creation and editing within a single framework. Motion-control methods such as MagicMotion ( Li et al., 2025 ) inject trajectory conditions through a ControlNet-style branch and achieve effective object-motion control, but this design introduces a relatively heavy conditional pathway and assumes explicit trajectory or region-level controls. These methods work well when the desired change can be specified through text, inversion trajectories, reference conditions, or reliable correspondences, but they often struggle with exemplar-specific appearance changes, global relighting, or complex local edits without masks. EditDistill instead replaces implicit prompt interpretation and dense control specification with an explicit learned transformation descriptor while relying on the video backbone for temporal rendering. Compared with ControlNet-style residual branches ( Zhang et al., 2023 ) , and low-rank adapters ( Hu et al., 2022 ) , our injector follows this parameter-efficient design but focus more on the diffusion process.

paragraphs.en: EditDistill contains two components trained sequentially. Stage I learns an image edit descriptor that captures the transformation between a before/after image pair. Stage II uses this descriptor to condition a video diffusion model. paragraphs.en: The edit descriptor together with the residual reconstruction encourages a separation of roles: z s z^{s} preserves the shared content, while 𝐝 \mathbf{d} captures the edit-specific change. The attention maps in Fig. 4 help reveal what 𝐝 \mathbf{d} encodes. For local edits, high responses concentrate on regions that need to change ( e.g. , object parts or inserted attributes), while background remains largely unaffected. For global edits such as illumination or style changes, the responses become broader but still focus on meaningful regions like the sky, light sources, and main scene elements, rather than spreading uniformly. These patterns indicate that 𝐝 \mathbf{d} does not represent a target image or a fixed mask. Instead, it specifies what transformation to apply , while its interaction with video features determines where the change is applied in each frame as illustrated by the frame-wise descriptor attention maps in Fig. 8 . This separation allows the edit to transfer consistently across frames without explicit mask supervision, while preserving unaffected regions.

paragraphs.en: Stage I uses approximately 2M paired images aggregated from OmniGen2 and GPT-Image-Edit ( Wu et al., 2025b ; Wang et al., 2025c ) . For stage II, We carefully constructed a large-scale video editing dataset. First, we leveraged the Wan 2.1 video generation model to synthesize preliminary video pairs from image editing pair data, while strictly enforcing identical text prompts except for the edited regions. To further improve the consistency of these coarse video-editing pairs, we use the edit loss and DINO feature loss described in the Method section, which effectively constrained both semantic and structural alignment between these video pairs. After a rigorous filtering process, we ultimately obtained 100K high-quality video editing samples. In addition, for the training data, we also constructed paired samples from the OpenVid ( Nan et al., 2024 ) dataset by randomly injecting noise into videos and randomly shuffling video frames, using the original real videos as reconstruction targets.
paragraphs.zh: 第一阶段使用了约 200 万对图像，这些图像由 OmniGen2 和 GPT-Image-Edit（Wu et al., 2025b；Wang et al., 2025c）汇总而来。 对于第二阶段，我们精心构建了一个大规模的视频编辑数据集。 首先，我们利用 Wan 2.1 视频生成模型从图像编辑对数据中合成初步的视频对，同时严格保证除被编辑区域外文本提示词完全一致。 为了进一步提升这些粗糙视频编辑对的一致性，我们使用方法章节中描述的编辑损失和 DINO 特征损失，这有效约束了这些视频对之间的语义和结构对齐。 经过严格的筛选流程，我们最终获得了 10 万个高质量的视频编辑样本。 此外，对于训练数据，我们还基于 OpenVid（Nan et al., 2024）数据集构建了配对样本，方法是对视频随机注入噪声并随机打乱视频帧，同时以原始真实视频作为重建目标。

Preservation is measured by DINO-sim on regions outside the edit estimated by Grounded-SAM2 ( Ren et al., 2024 ; Ravi et al., 2024 ; Oquab et al., 2023 ) . Temporal coherence is assessed using CLIP-based adjacent-frame consistency (Temp.) and optical-flow warp error (Warp) ( Huang et al., 2024 ) , while perceptual quality is measured by FVD ( Unterthiner et al., 2019 ) . We further report VBench-style metrics, including subject consistency (SubC), background consistency (BkgC), motion smoothness (MoS), aesthetic quality (AesQ), and dynamic degree (DyaD), for the consistency of video quality. paragraphs.en: Fig. 5 provides a qualitative comparison that helps explain the differences behind the above metrics. Prompt-driven methods often capture the coarse caption but miss small exemplar-specific attributes, such as accessories or fine texture changes. Frame-wise and inversion-based methods can make a sharper local change in the first few frames, but the edit may jitter, weaken, or contaminate nearby regions as the clip evolves. Reference-conditioned methods better preserve the target appearance, yet they sometimes transfer irrelevant color or texture from the reference image into the background. EditDistill is more stable because the image pair defines a transformation rather than a target appearance: the distilled transformation feature 𝐝 \mathbf{d} indicates what should change, and cross-attention to video tokens determines where the change should be applied.
paragraphs.zh: 图 5 给出了定性对比，有助于解释上述指标背后的差异。 基于提示词的方法往往只能捕捉粗略的描述，而遗漏示例特有的细节属性，例如配饰或细微的纹理变化。 逐帧方法和基于反演的方法可以在前几帧中实现更锐利的局部变化，但随着视频片段的推进，编辑效果可能抖动、减弱或污染附近区域。 基于参考条件的方法能更好地保留目标外观，但有时会把参考图像中不相关的颜色或纹理迁移到背景中。 EditDistill 更加稳定，因为图像对定义的是一种变换而非目标外观：蒸馏得到的变换特征 𝐝 \mathbf{d} 指示应当改变什么，而对视频 token 的交叉注意力则决定变化应应用在哪里。

paragraphs.en: The results show a consistent pattern. Strong video priors can be smooth but under-edit; strong image or inversion control can edit individual frames but lose temporal stability; reference-conditioned methods improve appearance transfer but may copy irrelevant details. EditDistill improves this trade-off by representing the user intent as a compact transformation descriptor and injecting it directly into the denoising dynamics of a frozen video backbone, enabling controllable edits with temporal coherence and structural consistency.

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we propose EditDistill , a two-stage framework for transformation-guided video editing that distills image-level editing description into a compact feature and injects it into a video diffusion model. By guiding the denoising process with this feature, together with edit-descriptor alignment and DINO structural consistency losses for temporal consistency, our method enables controllable video editing while preserving the generative prior of the backbone. Our framework provides a practical paradigm for integrating image-level editing into video generation, with potential applications in content creation, video post-production, and interactive media editing.
paragraphs.zh: 在本文中，我们提出 EditDistill，一个用于变换引导视频编辑的两阶段框架，它将图像级编辑描述蒸馏为紧凑特征，并将其注入视频扩散模型。 通过使用该特征引导去噪过程，并结合用于时间一致性的编辑描述符对齐损失和 DINO 结构一致性损失，我们的方法在保留骨干网络生成先验的同时实现可控视频编辑。 我们的框架为将图像级编辑融入视频生成提供了实用范式，在内容创作、视频后期制作和交互式媒体编辑方面具有潜在应用价值。

paragraphs.en: The projected feature is processed by a multi-scale hierarchy. Each scale contains two residual blocks, a transformer block, and a downsampling operation; this sequence is repeated three times. Local residual blocks preserve fine edit evidence, the downsampling path enlarges the receptive field, and transformer blocks allow non-local interactions between changed and unchanged regions. paragraphs.zh: 共享的词干（stem）隔离了阶段 I 潜空间（1024 维，为图像对重建而优化）与视频 DiT 的逐块残差流（根据块的不同为 4096–6144 维，为时空去噪而优化）之间的基变换。 在各分支之间共享这一词干使可训练参数数量保持在较小水平，并起到软正则化的作用，防止每个分支对 d d 学出私有的、相互冲突的解释。

paragraphs.en: The cross-attention branch lets the hidden sequence h ∈ ℝ T × D h\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times D} attend to the adapted code d ¯ \bar{d} as a global edit token,

paragraphs.en: Because the spatial query side decides where to attend on a per-token basis, this branch is the natural fit for spatially selective edits (object-local color changes, identity swaps in a face region, accessory addition). It also inherits the spatial re-localization property of the Stage I attention: the same d ¯ \bar{d} produces a different attention mask on each frame, so the edit follows the moving content.
